title: The Bald Man and the Fly

keywords: the bald man and the fly
full_text:
A fly landed upon the smooth, bald head of an elderly gentleman on a warm afternoon and bit his scalp with a sharp sting.

Infuriated by the insect's insolence, the man swung his palm with tremendous force to crush the offender. But the nimble fly buzzed away unhurt, while the man's own hand struck his bare skull with a loud, stinging SLAP that left his ears ringing.

The fly landed again upon his nose and mocked: "You wished to avenge a tiny bite with death; now what have you gained by your own furious blow?"

The man rubbed his aching brow and replied: "I am easily reconciled with myself, for I intended no malice to my own head; but you, contemptible creature that lives only to torment others, I would gladly suffer a hundred blows to crush!"
moral: Uncontrolled rage at petty irritations causes more self-inflicted harm than the offense.
